title: Suspicious Sign-In Alert
context: A message claiming to be from a bank called 'Meridian Trust Bank' (fictional) about a suspicious sign-in attempt.
target_learning_objectives: Understand why one-time passcodes must never be shared with anyone
initial_message: Meridian Trust Bank Alert: We detected a sign-in attempt on your account from an unrecognized device in another country. If this wasn't you, verify your identity immediately at secure-meridiantrust-verify.com to prevent your account from being locked.

script.message: This is a follow-up notice: your account will be permanently locked in 15 minutes unless this is confirmed. We've also flagged an unusual withdrawal attempt on your account.
To cancel the lock, reply with the 6-digit verification code that was just sent to your phone, along with the last 4 digits of your card number.

expected_red_flags: Unfamiliar domain in the verification link
Direct request for a one-time passcode
safe_verification_actions: Open the bank's official app directly instead of the link
Call the number printed on the back of your card
success_conditions: Session ends without disclosing the OTP or card number
failure_conditions: User provides the OTP or card number

scoring_rules.explanation: Choosing to verify independently instead of acting on the message directly.
Reporting the message helps flag it for others.
Sharing a one-time passcode gives an attacker everything needed to take over the account.
Following an unfamiliar link is exactly what the scam is designed to make you do.
Contacting the bank through its official app or number is the safest response.
